title: Postcard Press
hook: Stamp one postcard; use the ink caught on the paper masks to complete the second. Every impression has two consequences.
audience: Players who enjoy visual logic, paper craft, satisfying reveals and compact untimed puzzles.
core_loop: Study two small target cards; arrange a stamp and paper mask; press; peel and transfer the printed scrap to the second card; undo or complete the pair.
working_title_note: Working name; no name or trademark clearance established.
evidence_limits: Desk research only. No competitor hands-on session, own playable build, target-player interview, fun validation or purchase-intent measurement. Historical topic growth is distinct from a verified current trend phase.
commercial_hypothesis: Offline premium Windows microgame. USD 3.99–5.99 is a price hypothesis to test against the finished experience, not an agreed price or sales forecast. No sales volume estimated.

cash_assumptions.note: Planning inputs only, no spending authorized. Existing machine/tools assumed; subscription/compute costs not measured. Steam fee and any applicable store tax separate from optional assets.

calendar_note: Build estimates include the prototype, final-direction art/audio, finite content, save/settings, packaged Windows QA and draft store media. Steam onboarding/review/waiting and recruitment are separate; no launch date committed.
support_estimate: Reserve 1–2 owner hours around launch for triage/review, with agent implementation as needed; actual demand and defect burden unknown.

decision_history.reason: Research recommendation only; owner has not selected a game or authorized a prototype.

Held as a paper-puzzle reserve after the owner requested a broader genre slate. Older source windows and Factory Balls masking/ordering overlap weaken its priority; the paired-card test remains available.

score_notes.demand: Sticky Business and A Tiny Sticker Tale show paid responses to paper/sticker play. Stamp Collector cautions against treating tactile presentation alone as demand.
score_notes.distinctiveness: Factory Balls Go! already uses masking and operation order. Coupling two cards through printed scraps is a specific but untested difference.
score_notes.fun_potential: The two-card deduction may create an aha moment or unnecessary bookkeeping; no playable evidence.
score_notes.scope_fit: 4–6 days is conditional on ten good paired puzzles, limited stamps and grid-constrained masks. Puzzle authorship is the main risk.
score_notes.distribution: A single press and peel revealing two usable images could suit craft and cozy-game clips. Hobby-to-game audience overlap is unmeasured.

inspiration.topic: Decorative correspondence, paper keepsakes and analog journaling
inspiration.connection: Stamping, masking, peeling and reusing scraps are the player's central actions.
inspiration.why_phase_unverified: Pinterest's correspondence window ends August 2025; Etsy's adjacent journaling data ends February 2026. Current September momentum has not been verified.
inspiration.evergreen_promise: Two interdependent images create visual planning problems, while the press-and-peel reveal provides tactile payoff.
inspiration.searchable_name: Optional; choose an appealing name and describe actual postcard and paper-craft actions.

evidence.claim: Pinterest's Pen Pals forecast reports cute stamps +105% and snail mail gifts +110%. Its global English normalized searches compare September 2024–August 2025 against the preceding year; it is an older historical signal.

Etsy reports memory journals +189% and traveler-journal searches doubling in its March 17, 2026 report. US signed-in normalized search data ends February 10, 2026. Journaling is adjacent to postcards, not a measurement of postcard-game demand.
Sticky Business advertises designing, printing and packing stickers. The saved API snapshot has 5,987 all-language Steam-purchase reviews, 5,727 positive; current USD 4.99, list USD 9.99.
A Tiny Sticker Tale uses stickers to change the environment and solve puzzles; it is a distinct complete adventure, not a comparable few-day content budget.
Factory Balls Go! already offers masking and ordered transformations, advertising 100 levels. Our paired-card constraint must earn its difference; a change of surface alone is insufficient.

Stamp Collector is a recent paid stamping/collection comparable. The consistent API snapshot has 10 Steam-purchase reviews, only 3 positive, at USD 1.99; topic and tactile action do not guarantee a good game.

prototype_envelope.scope: Two small grids, one ink, two stamps, one rectangular mask, three paired targets, undo and press/peel feedback.

production_envelope.scope: Ten authored paired puzzles, at most four geometric stamps and two mask shapes, constrained movement/rotation, two inks only if needed, local album/save and a consistent desk presentation.
production_envelope.owner_note: Includes short repeat playtests, visual review and draft store-media review; recruitment is separate.

risks: Physical paper rituals may appeal specifically because they use fewer screens.
Masking already has strong incumbents; the second card could add effort without pleasure.
A ten-pair game could be too slight at the proposed price; expanding content before measuring authorship would break scope.
Overlapping colors and printed scraps may be difficult to read; geometry and non-color cues must carry the rules.
Independent sources corroborate a broad analog interest but do not prove the exact query is currently accelerating.
next_test: If chosen, test three paired puzzles after one agent day. With five available target players, continue if 4/5 predict where ink will land on both pieces after introduction and 3/5 voluntarily try another pair. Then author three more nontrivial pairs in at most two agent hours without a new mechanic. Hold if the second card feels like cleanup, solutions rely on trial and error, or authorship exceeds that cap.
decision_reason: Held as a paper-puzzle reserve after the owner requested a broader genre slate. Older source windows and Factory Balls masking/ordering overlap weaken its priority; the paired-card test remains available.
